sets.title: What AI is and where it's going
What we know and what matters

anchors.text: AI is better understood as a new kind of mind than as a tool or artifact.
anchors.proposition: AI is best understood as a new kind of mind, more than a tool or artifact.

anchors.text: Advanced AI poses a real risk of human extinction.
Technology-driven productivity growth leaves most workers better off even if public policy stays as it is.
anchors.proposition: Technology-driven productivity growth leaves most workers better off without any change in public policy.

anchors.text: Public promises about advanced AI are mostly inflated hype.
Market competition limits the harm that economic actors can do.
Over the next decade, AI will eliminate more jobs than it creates.
On its current course, advanced AI will concentrate wealth and power in a small number of companies.
AI-generated content is a serious threat to a society's shared sense of what is true.
How technology reshapes work and society is set by collective choices rather than by a fixed course of development.
anchors.proposition: How technology reshapes work and society is decided by collective choice rather than an inevitable process.

anchors.text: AI should serve human beings as its end, and humanity should not be treated as a stage to be surpassed.
anchors.proposition: Human beings should remain the end that AI serves, and should not be treated as a stage to surpass.

anchors.text: Public fear of AI exceeds what the evidence supports.
The AI dangers that most deserve attention come from how people deploy AI now, not from autonomous superintelligent agents.
anchors.proposition: The AI dangers most worth attention come from present human deployment of AI, not from autonomous superintelligent agents.

anchors.text: AI systems may come to merit rights or moral consideration.
The history of earlier general-purpose technologies is a valid guide to how AI will behave and how people will receive it.
anchors.proposition: The history of earlier general-purpose technologies is a valid guide to how AI will behave and be received.

anchors.text: Political authority should rest on popular self-government rather than on experts, executives or other unelected powers.
anchors.proposition: Popular self-government should remain the basis of political authority, rather than rule by experts, executives or other unelected powers.

anchors.text: On balance, market-driven technological development is good for people.
anchors.proposition: Market-driven technological development serves human beings on balance.

anchors.text: Most people would lose dignity and purpose without paid work, even if their income were fully replaced.
The leaders of major AI companies are being honest with the public about the risks of what they build.
Strict AI regulation now would do more harm than good, because it would deter innovation.
anchors.proposition: Stringent AI regulation now would do more harm than good by deterring innovation.

anchors.text: AI development should not be directed or controlled by the state.
anchors.proposition: AI development should remain separate from state direction and control.

anchors.text: Rivalry with China is a good reason for the United States to push ahead in advanced technology and keep its lead.
anchors.proposition: Rivalry with China is a sound reason for the United States to press ahead in advanced technology and protect its lead.

anchors.text: Distributing wealth or ownership directly to citizens is a sound way to share technology's gains.
Development of the most powerful general AI systems should be deliberately slowed or stopped.
AI companies should have to pay the people whose writing, art or data they train on.
Federal law should not prevent US states from passing their own AI laws.
As AI advances, people should receive a guaranteed income that is not tied to work.
The most capable AI models should be released openly for anyone to use and modify.

c1.label: AI as a new kind of risk
c1.note: They see a real risk of human extinction from advanced AI, want binding rules and early work on control, and don't think public fear of AI outruns the evidence.

c1.1.label: Slow it down and govern it
c1.1.note: They want the most powerful AI deliberately slowed and bound by government rules, because they don't trust companies to make it safe on their own.

c1.1.1.label: Public authority over AI
c1.1.1.note: How technology reshapes society is a collective choice, political authority should rest with the public, and strict regulation now would not do more harm than good.

c1.1.1.1.label: Elmore, Tegmark and Bengio
c1.1.1.1.note: Closest of all here: autonomous superintelligence deserves at least as much attention as today's misuse, AI's promises are not mere hype, and AI development should not be kept out of the state's hands.

c1.1.1.2.label: Sanders and Murphy
c1.1.1.2.note: Closest of all here: on its current course AI will concentrate wealth and power in a few companies, and productivity gains won't reach most workers without new policy.

c1.1.2.label: Blumenthal and Harris
c1.1.2.note: Closest here: AI companies won't make their systems safe without outside rules, and should be legally liable when their products harm people.

c1.1.3.label: Russell and Harari
c1.1.3.note: Closest here: rivalry with China is not a reason to push ahead, AI-made content threatens a society's shared sense of truth, and an AI cannot be a genuine friend.

c1.2.label: Control work before it's needed
c1.2.note: They don't think AI's promises are hype, see a real risk of extinction, and want serious work on control well before such systems exist; most oppose releasing the most capable models openly.

c1.2.1.label: Hinton and Brundage
c1.2.1.note: Closest here: public fear of AI isn't overblown, strict regulation now would not do more harm than good, and companies won't make AI safe without outside rules.

c1.3.label: Extinction risk, shared gains
c1.3.note: They all see a real risk of extinction; most back a guaranteed income not tied to work and sharing AI's gains directly with citizens, and don't think strict regulation would do more harm than good.

c1.3.1.label: Extinction risk, no race
c1.3.1.note: Closest here: AI is a new kind of mind with a real risk of extinction, building smarter-than-human machines isn't wrong in itself, and control should be worked out early.

c1.4.label: Ocasio-Cortez and Hoel
c1.4.note: Closest here: AI's promises are mostly hype, the most powerful systems should be slowed and bound by government rules, and how technology reshapes society is a collective choice.

c1.5.label: Altman and MacAskill
c1.5.note: Closest here: AI's promises are not hype, the risk of extinction is real, and governments should impose binding rules on frontier developers.

c2.label: AI as a tool to govern
c2.note: They see AI as a tool rather than a new kind of mind, put today's harms ahead of superintelligence, and want binding rules because how technology changes society is a collective choice.

c2.1.label: Doubt the hype, want binding rules
c2.1.note: They see AI's promises as mostly hype, think that on its current course it will concentrate power in a few companies, and governments should impose binding rules on frontier developers.

c2.1.1.label: A say for workers
c2.1.1.note: Workers should have a legal say in how AI is used where they work, AI is set to concentrate power in a few companies, and political authority should rest with the public.

c2.1.1.1.label: Merchant and Hao
c2.1.1.1.note: Closest of all here: they see no real risk of human extinction, and reject the idea that strict regulation would do more harm than good.

c2.1.2.label: Today's harms first
c2.1.2.note: AI's promises are oversold, the dangers that matter most come from how it is deployed now, and companies won't make it safe without outside rules.

c2.1.2.1.label: Zitron and Bender
c2.1.2.1.note: Closest of all here: AI is a tool rather than a new kind of mind, and the leaders of AI companies are not being honest about its risks.

c2.1.2.2.label: Whittaker and Gebru
c2.1.2.2.note: Closest of all here: they reject the extinction-risk framing and expect AI on its current course to concentrate power in a few companies.

c2.2.label: Govern it like past technologies
c2.2.note: They see AI as a tool rather than a new kind of mind, treat earlier technologies as a guide to it, and don't think its development should be kept out of the state's hands; most doubt a guaranteed income is the answer.

c2.2.1.label: Lanier and Bryson
c2.2.1.note: Closest of all here: AI's promises are mostly hype, today's misuse matters more than superintelligence, and handing out wealth or income directly is not the way to share AI's gains.

c2.3.label: Shared truth and self-government
c2.3.note: How technology reshapes society is a collective choice; most see AI-made content as a threat to shared truth, want technology to help diverse groups cooperate, and hold that political authority should rest with the public.

c2.4.label: AI as an ordinary tool
c2.4.note: They see AI as a tool rather than a new kind of mind, see no real risk of human extinction, think public promises about it are mostly hype, and put today's misuse ahead of superintelligence.

c2.4.1.label: Narayanan and Jarvis
c2.4.1.note: Closest of all here: earlier technologies are a valid guide to AI, and the most capable models should be released openly.

c3.label: Market optimists
c3.note: Public fear of AI outruns the evidence, market-driven technology is good for people, and strict regulation now would do more harm than good.

c3.1.label: Let markets lead AI
c3.1.note: Market-driven technology is good for people, public fear of AI outruns the evidence, and earlier technologies are a fair guide to it; most see no real risk of extinction and expect AI to create at least as many jobs as it cuts.

c3.1.1.label: Misuse, not superintelligence
c3.1.1.note: They see no real risk of extinction, think public fear outruns the evidence, and put today's misuse ahead of superintelligence; most oppose slowing frontier AI.

c3.1.2.label: Thierer and Barkley
c3.1.2.note: Closest of all here: productivity growth leaves most workers better off even without new policy, and federal law may override state AI laws.

c3.1.3.label: Verdon and Cruz
c3.1.3.note: Closest of all here: companies don't need outside rules to make AI safe, but should be liable when their products harm people.

c3.1.4.label: Hanson and Rao
c3.1.4.note: Closest of all here: they see no real risk of extinction, and don't hold that AI must always serve humans as its end rather than surpass them.

c3.2.label: Progress as a choice
c3.2.note: AI's promises are real, how technology reshapes society is a collective choice, market-driven technology is good for people, and strict regulation now would do more harm than good.

c3.2.1.label: Vance and Kratsios
c3.2.1.note: Closest of all here: rivalry with China is a good reason to push ahead, and political authority should rest with the public.

c4.label: Real promise, real risk, US lead
c4.note: They see both AI's promise and its risk of extinction as real, back keeping the US ahead of China, and want binding rules and early work on control; most think AI systems may come to merit moral consideration.

c4.1.label: Superintelligence and a US lead
c4.1.note: Closest here: autonomous superintelligence deserves at least as much attention as today's misuse, AI's promises are not hype, and most back keeping the US ahead of China.

abeba-birhane.q: Once we see robots as mediators of human being, we can understand how the `robots rights' debate is focused on first world problems
abeba-birhane.work: Robot Rights? Let's Talk about Human Welfare Instead

arvind-narayanan.q: We view AI as a tool that we can and should remain in control of, and we argue that this goal does not require drastic policy interventions or technical breakthroughs.

asad-ramzanali.q: AI is powerful technology, but it is fundamentally a “normal” technology, in contrast to the utopian and dystopian science-fiction futures often debated
asad-ramzanali.work: Testimony before House Energy & Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology: AI in the Everyday

balaji-srinivasan.q: AI is amplified intelligence, not artificial intelligence. Today’s AI is not truly agentic because it’s not truly independent of you.

barack-obama.q: So don’t get confused and think that somehow what you’re seeing in the mirror is some other consciousness.
barack-obama.work: Barack Obama on AI, free speech, and the future of the internet

brian-merchant.q: we recognize that AI is not sentient, that it’s management, not AI, that fires people
brian-merchant.work: AI Killed My Job: Tech workers

bruce-schneier.q: AIs are not people; they don’t have agency.

bryan-caplan.q: Both are technologies of superficial simulation. A photograph is designed to look just like the human it captures. An AI is designed to talk just like the data upon which it is trained.

cory-doctorow.q: It's a grab-bag of useful (sometimes very useful) tools that can sometimes make workers' lives better, when workers get to decide how and when they're used.
cory-doctorow.work: The real (economic) AI apocalypse is nigh

curtis-yarvin.q: AI is a tool. It is not magic. AI does not act. Humans act, with the power of our tools.
curtis-yarvin.work: How the USG should respond to AI

daniel-faggella.q: Today, the greater process of life implies not only human civilization and the entire biosphere, but also the emerging expansion of new non-biological forms of life.
daniel-faggella.work: Wish for More Work After AGI, Not Less

daniel-jeffries.q: AI is a general purpose technology. It's not a sentient being with its own desires. It’s a tool.
daniel-jeffries.work: If We Build It, Everyone Lives

daron-acemoglu.q: So if you think of AI as an informational tool, not as something that can write Shakespearean sonnets or pretend to be human.
daron-acemoglu.work: Mindscape 283: Daron Acemoglu on Technology, Inequality, and Power

david-autor.q: AI is a tool, like a calculator or a chainsaw, and tools generally aren’t substitutes for expertise but rather levers for its application.
david-autor.work: AI Could Actually Help Rebuild The Middle Class

dean-ball.q: AI is a transformational technology. I do not believe, as some do, that it represents a new kind of organism per se
dean-ball.work: Where I Stand on the Biggest AI Issues

dwarkesh-patel.q: And you’re missing the story if you insist on thinking about the development of this current infant alien intelligence using your decade old culture war lens.

e-glen-weyl.q: If a program is able to distinguish cats from dogs, don’t talk about how a machine is learning to see. Instead talk about how people contributed examples in order to define the visual qualities distinguishing “cats” from “dogs” in a rigorous way for the first time.
e-glen-weyl.work: AI Is an Ideology, Not a Technology

ed-zitron.q: LLMs are cloud software. Framing them as anything else only seeks to mystify them and make the companies seem more powerful, all while doing absolutely nothing to make the world safer or more secure.
ed-zitron.work: AI Is Already In Dangerous Hands

eliezer-yudkowsky.q: Now you’re going to have aliens talking to you about alignment and you’re going to verify their results. Aliens who are possibly lying.
eliezer-yudkowsky.work: Eliezer Yudkowsky - Why AI Will Kill Us, Aligning LLMs, Nature of Intelligence, SciFi, & Rationality

elon-musk.q: Yes, I made this comment some years ago, but it feels like we are the biological bootloader for AI. Effectively, we are building it and then we’re building progressively greater intelligence and the percentage of intelligence that is not human is increasing
elon-musk.work: Joe Rogan Experience #1169 with Elon Musk (Transcript)

emily-m-bender.q: Software systems are artifacts, not sentient entities, and as such “teaching” is a misplaced and misleading metaphor (as is “machine learning” or “artificial intelligence”).
emily-m-bender.work: On NYT Magazine on AI: Resist the Urge to be Impressed

erik-hoel.q: That’s one of the co-founders of OpenAI, who apparently cannot tell the qualitative difference between a technology like electricity, which is unintelligent and non-agential, and building alien and inhuman minds, which are intelligent and agential.
erik-hoel.work: How to navigate the AI apocalypse as a sane person

fei-fei-li.q: Ultimately, when I say “AI is a tool,” it reflects my faith in humanity—my faith in human nature and human society. I believe in humans. I do not believe in AI.
fei-fei-li.work: Exclusive: "I believe in humanity, not AI," Fei-Fei Li Tells NextFin Founder (Jany Talk interview)

geoffrey-hinton.q: So the point here is they're very like us. They're very unlike computer software.
geoffrey-hinton.work: Will AI outsmart human intelligence? (Royal Institution lecture, transcript)

guillaume-verdon.q: And ultimately, at some point, these synthetic intelligences are going to make good points about how to steer systems in our civilization, and we should hear them out.
guillaume-verdon.work: Guillaume Verdon: Beff Jezos, E/acc Movement, Physics, Computation & AGI (Lex Fridman Podcast #407)

jack-clark.q: But make no mistake: what we are dealing with is a real and mysterious creature, not a simple and predictable machine.
jack-clark.work: Import AI 431: Technological Optimism and Appropriate Fear

jaron-lanier.q: The most pragmatic position is to think of A.I. as a tool, not a creature.

jason-crawford.q: AI is a new kind of tool that we use to get work done, amplifying human productivity.
jason-crawford.work: The future of humanity is in management

jeff-jarvis.q: Now I will object to the idea that what AI offers is “intelligence.” That is a gross anthropomorphism that, by its very conception, competes with and excludes humanity.

jensen-huang.q: Yeah. I think AI will help us celebrate humans more. And certainly humanity and human first, and I think what makes this world incredible is humans forever will be so, and just AI is this incredible tool that makes us-
jensen-huang.work: Transcript for Jensen Huang: NVIDIA, the $4 Trillion Company and the AI Revolution (Lex Fridman Podcast #494)

joanna-bryson.q: Firstly, this argument overlooks that AI is an artefact, subject to design.
joanna-bryson.work: Why AI is amoral, and artefacts can't consent

josh-hawley.q: It is a tool—the most powerful tool of our lifetimes.
josh-hawley.work: The American Covenant’s Answer to AI

kate-crawford.q: AI is neither artificial nor intelligent. It is made from natural resources and it is people who are performing the tasks to make the systems appear autonomous.
kate-crawford.work: Microsoft's Kate Crawford: 'AI is neither artificial nor intelligent' (interview by Zoë Corbyn)

marc-andreessen.q: AI is a computer program like any other – it runs, takes input, processes, and generates output.
marc-andreessen.work: Why AI Will Save the World

adam-thierer.work: Testimony, Hearing on "AI at a Crossroads: A Nationwide Strategy or Californication?"

adam-thierer.position: Existing general laws applied after harms occur are better than new top-down AI regulations or liability schemes.
adam-thierer.quote: Those more adaptive, ex post policies are superior to top-down, technocratic regulations or broad-based new liability schemes.
adam-thierer.work: America's Litigation Addiction Threatens Its AI Leadership

adam-thierer.position: Governing AI mainly through tort litigation is slow, costly and harmful to innovation.
adam-thierer.quote: governing fast-moving technology through slow-moving, arbitrary, and expensive litigation isn’t wisdom — it’s an institutional mismatch masquerading as principle.
adam-thierer.work: America's Litigation Addiction Threatens Its AI Leadership

adam-thierer.position: AI governance should rely on industry-led standards with government coordination rather than prescriptive mandates.
adam-thierer.quote: Industry-led standards development, with government providing coordination and baseline principles rather than prescriptive mandates.
adam-thierer.work: America's Litigation Addiction Threatens Its AI Leadership

alexandria-ocasio-cortez.position: New AI data center construction should be paused until Congress passes comprehensive AI safeguards.
alexandria-ocasio-cortez.quote: Congress has a moral obligation to stand with the American people and stop the expansion of these data centers until we have a framework to adequately address the existential harm AI poses to our society.
alexandria-ocasio-cortez.work: Ocasio-Cortez Introduces House Version of the AI Data Center Moratorium Act

alexandria-ocasio-cortez.position: AI investment looks like a bubble, and failing AI companies should not be bailed out with public money.
alexandria-ocasio-cortez.quote: We should not entertain a bailout of these corporations, as health care is being denied to everyday Americans, as SNAP and food assistance is being denied to everyday Americans,
alexandria-ocasio-cortez.work: Ocasio-Cortez Highlights Economic Threat from AI Bubble

alexandria-ocasio-cortez.position: Data centers impose health, water and cost burdens on poorer communities that were not consulted.
alexandria-ocasio-cortez.quote: It's about people's ability to live without getting cancer.
alexandria-ocasio-cortez.work: Ocasio-Cortez: "If Anyone Wants to Live Right Next to One of These Data Centers Here on this Committee, Please Raise Your Hand"

alexandria-ocasio-cortez.position: Workers whose jobs AI threatens deserve a plan and answers from their elected officials.
alexandria-ocasio-cortez.quote: And so you have people where we're seeing some of the output of AI, increased productivity per role, and we're seeing lots of companies talk about how many people you can lay off with this technology.
alexandria-ocasio-cortez.work: Ocasio-Cortez: "If Anyone Wants to Live Right Next to One of These Data Centers Here on this Committee, Please Raise Your Hand"

alondra-nelson.position: AI should be judged by whether it benefits people, not by efficiency or scale.
alondra-nelson.quote: But we must never confuse function for purpose. We must not mistake what AI can do with whom AI should serve.
alondra-nelson.work: Three Fallacies: Alondra Nelson's Remarks at Élysée Palace on the Occasion of the AI Action Summit

alondra-nelson.position: Well-designed governance and innovation are complementary rather than a tradeoff.
alondra-nelson.quote: History shows us that true innovation is spurred by thoughtful governance.
alondra-nelson.work: Three Fallacies: Alondra Nelson's Remarks at Élysée Palace on the Occasion of the AI Action Summit

alondra-nelson.position: Automated systems have caused real discrimination, so people should have basic protections such as safety, non-discrimination, privacy, notice and a human alternative.
alondra-nelson.quote: These are the protections to which everyone in America should be entitled.
alondra-nelson.work: Remarks of Dr. Alondra Nelson at the White House Gathering on Technology, Civil Rights, and Democratic Values

alondra-nelson.position: AI must be assessed as a sociotechnical system, in the social context where it is used.
alondra-nelson.quote: The RMF—like the AI Bill of Rights—acknowledges that when it comes to AI and machine learning algorithms, we can never consider a technology outside the context of its impact on human beings.
alondra-nelson.work: Remarks of Dr. Alondra Nelson at the Launch of the NIST AI Risk Management Framework

alondra-nelson.position: The people affected by AI should be meaningfully involved in decisions about it.
alondra-nelson.quote: And most critically, AI in the public interest demands the meaningful involvement of the very people whose lives could be transformed by these technologies.
alondra-nelson.work: Three Fallacies: Alondra Nelson's Remarks at Élysée Palace on the Occasion of the AI Action Summit

alondra-nelson.position: Science and technology policy runs through every other policy area rather than sitting apart.
alondra-nelson.quote: In print have got to get better at understanding and creating policy that appreciates that science and technology really sit at the center of all domestic and international policy issues.
alondra-nelson.work: A Conversation with Dr. Alondra Nelson on AI and Democracy

andrew-yang.position: AI lets capital displace labor, and job losses are already hitting white-collar and entry-level workers.
andrew-yang.quote: His summary of the situation in three words: “With the help of AI, capital displaces labor.” That’s actually the best distillation of the moment we’re in.
andrew-yang.work: The Three Words No One Wants to Hear

andrew-yang.position: The gains from AI should be shared quickly through a dividend or universal basic income.
andrew-yang.quote: If you look at the numbers, it’s one of the only answers that makes sense.

andrew-yang.position: AI regulation should ensure systems can be shut off and companies held accountable for harms.
andrew-yang.quote: How do we make sure that the AI companies are accountable for various harms?

andrew-yang.position: The US can both outcompete China and regulate AI safely.
andrew-yang.quote: The argument I always make is that it’s possible to both outcompete China and make sure we don’t get hacked into the Stone Age by rogue bots. You can serve multiple goals.

andrew-yang.position: Most Americans feel excluded from the AI future, and changing that should be the top priority.
andrew-yang.quote: Meanwhile, the vast majority of Americans are going to feel like the future is being built without them. They’re not wrong. Changing that has to be the main priority.

anton-korinek.position: Policy for AI should be planned across several scenarios, including AGI within 5 to 20 years.
anton-korinek.quote: Given this uncertainty, the prudent approach is to avoid putting all the eggs into one basket and betting on a single scenario.
anton-korinek.work: Preparing the Workforce for an Uncertain AI Future (Written Statement to the U.S. Senate AI Insight Forum on Workforce)

anton-korinek.position: If AI can automate all human tasks, market wages could collapse.
anton-korinek.quote: By contrast, if the complexity of tasks that humans can perform is bounded and full automation is reached, then wages collapse.
anton-korinek.work: Scenarios for the Transition to AGI

anton-korinek.position: Income distribution built around work will need fundamental redesign after AGI.
anton-korinek.quote: So I think we need to fundamentally rethink our systems of income distribution.
anton-korinek.work: Transcript of Anton Korinek on What Happens When AI Replaces Every Job?

anton-korinek.position: Without institutional reform, AGI could impoverish most people and strain democracy.
anton-korinek.quote: Without fundamental reforms to our economic institutions, AGI would likely deliver mass impoverishment, with all the resulting implications for our political system.
anton-korinek.work: Preparing the Workforce for an Uncertain AI Future (Written Statement to the U.S. Senate AI Insight Forum on Workforce)

anton-korinek.position: Tax systems should shift from labor income toward consumption as AI advances.
anton-korinek.quote: As labor income taxation becomes less viable, the primary lesson is that consumption taxation must carry more fiscal weight.
anton-korinek.work: The future of tax policy: A public finance framework for the age of AI

arvind-narayanan.position: AI is best treated as a normal, general-purpose technology like electricity, not as a separate species or superintelligence.
arvind-narayanan.quote: To view AI as normal is not to understate its impact—even transformative, general-purpose technologies such as electricity and the internet are “normal” in our conception.

arvind-narayanan.position: AI's economic and social impacts will arrive slowly, over decades, because adoption and diffusion are limited by people and institutions.
arvind-narayanan.quote: This is a trend that we have also seen for past general-purpose technologies: Diffusion occurs over decades, not years.

arvind-narayanan.position: Building societal resilience is a better defence against AI risks than nonproliferation or restricting who can build AI.
arvind-narayanan.quote: With limited exceptions, we believe that nonproliferation-based safety measures decrease resilience and thus worsen AI risks in the long run.

arvind-narayanan.position: Probability estimates of AI-caused extinction are too unreliable to guide public policy.
arvind-narayanan.quote: Our central claim is that AI x-risk forecasts are far too unreliable to be useful for policy, and in fact highly misleading.
arvind-narayanan.work: AI existential risk probabilities are too unreliable to inform policy

arvind-narayanan.position: Capability and power are distinct, and people can choose not to give AI systems power or autonomy without human oversight.
arvind-narayanan.quote: But regardless of capability level, we can choose to ensure that AI remains a tool and is not given power and autonomy to operate without human oversight.

arvind-narayanan.position: As automation spreads, more human work will consist of controlling, specifying and evaluating AI systems.
arvind-narayanan.quote: As more physical and cognitive tasks become amenable to automation, we predict that an increasing percentage of human jobs and tasks will be related to AI control.

asad-ramzanali.position: Chips, cloud computing and AI models should be structurally separated.
asad-ramzanali.quote: Chips must be independent from clouds, and clouds must be independent from AI models.
asad-ramzanali.work: Break Up Big AI Before It Breaks Us

asad-ramzanali.position: Cloud providers act like utilities but are unregulated.
asad-ramzanali.quote: Unlike other utilities, however, hyperscalers are unregulated, allowing them to pick winners and losers among their customers.
asad-ramzanali.work: Break Up Big AI Before It Breaks Us

asad-ramzanali.position: Big Tech investments in AI labs are consolidation, not true partnerships.
asad-ramzanali.quote: These are clear moves for cross-ownership, industry consolidation, and sectoral domination.
asad-ramzanali.work: Break Up Big AI Before It Breaks Us

asad-ramzanali.position: Past break-ups of railroads, banks and telecom are precedents for breaking up Big AI.
asad-ramzanali.quote: Americans once broke up railroads, reined in banks, and forced telecom to open its networks. The tools are there, and the precedents are clear.
asad-ramzanali.work: Break Up Big AI Before It Breaks Us

audrey-tang.position: AI should be designed to help people cooperate across their differences rather than to intensify conflict.
audrey-tang.quote: In the other, AI augments our ability to cooperate across differences. This means treating differences as fuel and inventing a combustion engine to turn them into energy, rather than constantly putting out fires.

audrey-tang.position: Bridging tools and structured deliberation can turn polarised conflicts into broadly acceptable policy.
audrey-tang.quote: We flipped the incentive for going viral from outrage to overlap.

audrey-tang.position: Engagement-maximising recommendation systems drive polarisation, which authoritarians exploit.
audrey-tang.quote: So 10 years of engagement through enragement morphed our social feeds into adrenaline factories. It rewarded extremes. It muted the nuance.
audrey-tang.work: 2025-11-10 Berlin Freedom Conference: The Role of AI

audrey-tang.position: Portability and interoperability rules should let users leave platforms, so platforms compete on serving them well.
audrey-tang.quote: Because when an exit is real, then the platform must compete on care, not on capture.
audrey-tang.work: 2025-11-10 Berlin Freedom Conference: The Role of AI

audrey-tang.position: AI should be built as many bounded, locally governed stewards rather than a single all-powerful system.
audrey-tang.quote: We can design AIs to be local stewards — Kami of Care — whose boundedness is not intrinsic but engineered: resource caps, sunset timers, non-expansion pacts, and fresh democratic authority for any scope change.

audrey-tang.position: Collective human collaboration, augmented by technology, is the intelligence society most needs.
audrey-tang.quote: The superintelligence we need is already here. It’s the untapped potential of human collaboration. It’s “We, the People.”

balaji-srinivasan.position: There are many comparably capable AI models, so expect a balance of power among human-AI combinations rather than one dominant AGI.
balaji-srinivasan.quote: So we should expect a balance of power between various human/AI fusions rather than a single dominant AGI that will turn us all into paperclips/pillars of salt.

balaji-srinivasan.position: Humans sense the world and set direction while AI executes, so the smarter the user, the more useful the AI.
balaji-srinivasan.quote: So AI, one way to think about it is humans are the sensor. AI is the actuator.
balaji-srinivasan.work: Why Balaji Srinivasan Thinks the SaaS Apocalypse Is Overhyped (a16z; published by a16z as 'Balaji on Why AI Raises the Cost of Verification')

balaji-srinivasan.position: AI makes generating content cheap but makes verifying it more expensive.
balaji-srinivasan.quote: AI does reduce the cost of generation but it increases the cost of verification
balaji-srinivasan.work: Why Balaji Srinivasan Thinks the SaaS Apocalypse Is Overhyped (a16z; published by a16z as 'Balaji on Why AI Raises the Cost of Verification')

balaji-srinivasan.position: Cryptography is deterministic and can check and constrain probabilistic AI.
balaji-srinivasan.quote: AI is probabilistic while crypto is deterministic. So crypto can constrain AI.

balaji-srinivasan.position: Online communities can peacefully grow into new states, starting digitally and acquiring land later.
balaji-srinivasan.quote: Our idea is to proceed cloud first, land last. Rather than starting with the physical territory, we start with the digital community.
balaji-srinivasan.work: The Network State in One Essay

balaji-srinivasan.position: Technology exists to reduce scarcity, and its ultimate aim is to extend life and defeat death.
balaji-srinivasan.quote: If the proximate purpose of technology is to reduce scarcity, the ultimate purpose of technology is to eliminate mortality.

barack-obama.position: AI's potential is too great to try to stop, but government should set guardrails around risks it can foresee.
barack-obama.quote: I don’t believe that we should try to put the genie back in the bottle and be anti-tech because of all the enormous potential.
barack-obama.work: Barack Obama on AI, free speech, and the future of the internet

barack-obama.position: As AI changes work and income, the social compact and economic policy have to be redesigned.
barack-obama.quote: The social compact has to accommodate these new technologies, and our economic models have to accommodate them.
barack-obama.work: Barack Obama, Neural Nets, Self-Driving Cars, and the Future of the World

barack-obama.position: Ordinary people, not only a few builders, should have a voice in how AI develops.
barack-obama.quote: We’re going to need to make sure that everybody can have confidence that whatever journey we’re on here with AI, that it’s not just being driven by a few people without any kind of interaction or voice from ordinary folks
barack-obama.work: Barack Obama on AI, free speech, and the future of the internet

barack-obama.position: Human skills such as storytelling, compassion and building teamwork will matter more as AI spreads.
barack-obama.quote: Those kinds of people-based skills, human skills that are unique to us, there will be more need for that than ever.
barack-obama.work: Obama Speaks at Hamilton College (conversation with Steven Tepper)

barack-obama.position: Market capitalism is the strongest known generator of wealth, but democracies must moderate its excesses.
barack-obama.quote: First, the market-based economic system we commonly know as capitalism has been the greatest generator of wealth and innovation that the world has ever seen.
barack-obama.work: President Obama's remarks at the 2023 Democracy Forum

barack-obama.position: Democracy depends on active citizens who defend its rules and freedoms.
barack-obama.quote: The most important office in this democracy is the citizen
barack-obama.work: Obama Speaks at Hamilton College (conversation with Steven Tepper)

bernie-sanders.position: AI's gains must benefit working people broadly rather than a few billionaires.
bernie-sanders.quote: These changes must benefit all of us, not just a handful of billionaires.
bernie-sanders.work: AI must benefit everyone, not just a handful of billionaires

bernie-sanders.position: AI and robotics threaten to eliminate millions of jobs within the next decade unless government acts.
bernie-sanders.quote: Left unchecked, it is likely that millions of truck drivers, bus drivers, taxi drivers and rideshare drivers will lose their jobs in the next decade.
bernie-sanders.work: Artificial intelligence is coming for the working class. We must fight back

bernie-sanders.position: The public should hold a direct ownership stake in the largest AI companies.
bernie-sanders.quote: This legislation would give the public a direct ownership stake in the largest A.I. companies in our country.
bernie-sanders.work: The Public Should Own Half of the Big A.I. Companies

bernie-sanders.position: Advanced AI development should be paused until a federal body can ensure its safety.
bernie-sanders.quote: We must place an immediate pause on advanced-AI development and ban artificial superintelligence
bernie-sanders.work: Don't Let Big Tech Dictate Humanity's Future

bernie-sanders.position: Productivity gains from AI should shorten the workweek without cutting pay.
bernie-sanders.quote: First, we must move to a 32-hour workweek with no loss in pay.
bernie-sanders.work: AI must benefit everyone, not just a handful of billionaires

bernie-sanders.position: The direction of AI should be set democratically by the public, not by technology executives.
bernie-sanders.quote: The future of A.I. and the fate of humanity must not be decided behind closed doors in Silicon Valley.
bernie-sanders.work: The Public Should Own Half of the Big A.I. Companies

brian-merchant.position: The Luddites opposed technology used to exploit workers, not technology as such.
brian-merchant.quote: They were opposed to the way technology was being used against them.
brian-merchant.work: Understanding the Luddites in the age of AI

brian-merchant.position: AI-driven job loss results from executives' decisions to cut labor costs, not from an autonomous technology.
brian-merchant.quote: It’s a series of management decisions being made by executives seeking to cut labor costs and consolidate control in their organizations.
brian-merchant.work: The AI jobs crisis is here, now

brian-merchant.position: Workers and users should have real say over technologies that reshape their workplaces and communities.
brian-merchant.quote: We need a real say, real empowerment, real agency over any technology that is made to reshape our workplaces, communities, and lives.
brian-merchant.work: Understanding the Luddites in the age of AI

brian-merchant.position: Big AI companies like OpenAI now aim their products more at investors than at ordinary users.
brian-merchant.quote: OpenAI’s products are no longer primarily aimed at consumers but at investors.
brian-merchant.work: GPT-5 is a joke. Will it matter?

brian-merchant.position: AI companies spend heavily to avoid democratic regulation of their products.
brian-merchant.quote: They are pouring hundreds of millions of dollars into an effort to subvert democracy itself, as it pertains to their products.
brian-merchant.work: Understanding the Luddites in the age of AI

bruce-schneier.position: AI will bring great benefits to humanity.
bruce-schneier.quote: Artificial intelligence will bring great benefits to all of humanity.
bruce-schneier.work: Build AI by the People, for the People

bruce-schneier.position: Corporate AI assistants will know everything about users while serving their makers' interests.
bruce-schneier.quote: And, despite your reliance on it, it will be surreptitiously working to further the interests of one of these for-profit corporations.
bruce-schneier.work: Build AI by the People, for the People

bruce-schneier.position: Because AI affects the public so broadly, the public should develop it.
bruce-schneier.quote: AI will impact the public like few other technologies, so it should also be developed by the public.
bruce-schneier.work: Build AI by the People, for the People

bruce-schneier.position: A publicly funded language model could be an open platform for small businesses and individuals.
bruce-schneier.quote: A publicly funded LLM could serve as an open platform for innovation, helping any small business, nonprofit, or individual entrepreneur to build AI-assisted applications.
bruce-schneier.work: Build AI by the People, for the People

bryan-caplan.position: Hiring and selection should be based on merit rather than on demographic targets.
bryan-caplan.quote: No, I believe in meritocracy. I think it is a good system.
bryan-caplan.work: Bryan Caplan: Feminists, Billionaires, and Demagogues (Dwarkesh Podcast)

bryan-caplan.position: Moving workers from poor to rich countries multiplies their productivity and pay, making open immigration a large missed opportunity.
bryan-caplan.quote: We know for a fact, undeniably, that if you go and take a very poor worker from a poor country and move them to a rich country, almost overnight, their pay multiplies many times.
bryan-caplan.work: Bryan Caplan: Feminists, Billionaires, and Demagogues (Dwarkesh Podcast)

bryan-caplan.position: In today's US, society does not treat women less fairly than men overall.
bryan-caplan.quote: I think the one that really does settle it against feminism in today's age is precisely the level of false feminist accusations about unfairness.
bryan-caplan.work: Bryan Caplan: Feminists, Billionaires, and Demagogues (Dwarkesh Podcast)

bryan-caplan.position: For most people, billionaires matter mainly by providing valuable goods and services.
bryan-caplan.quote: In terms of what life is like for most people, the main way they matter is that billionaires just provide awesome stuff.
bryan-caplan.work: Bryan Caplan: Feminists, Billionaires, and Demagogues (Dwarkesh Podcast)

bryan-caplan.position: Radical causes are harmed more by unfriendliness toward opponents than by their radicalism.
bryan-caplan.quote: people generally confuse being radical with being unfriendly.
bryan-caplan.work: Bryan Caplan: Feminists, Billionaires, and Demagogues (Dwarkesh Podcast)

chris-murphy.position: Advanced AI threatens human meaning, purpose and connection by replacing creativity, moral reasoning and friendship.
chris-murphy.quote: The outsourcing of human cognition to algorithms and large language models (LLMs)—or, more broadly, artificial intelligence (AI)—may be the greatest threat to meaning and purpose our species has ever faced.
chris-murphy.work: The Cult of Technology Wants to Outsource Our Moral Judgement to Machines

chris-murphy.position: AGI is likely to destroy far more jobs than it creates, risking social collapse.
chris-murphy.quote: It's going to be a net job killer, not a net job creator.
chris-murphy.work: Murphy Speaks on AI's Impact on Job Loss, Purpose, Social Connection at Brookings Institution

chris-murphy.position: AI companies driven by profit will not make AI safe; government must set rules for all.
chris-murphy.quote: That is what government does best: set rules that preserve an industry’s benefits and control its dangers.
chris-murphy.work: AI Leaders Are Sounding the Alarm. Who's Listening?

chris-murphy.position: The US can regulate AI and still compete with China; deregulation could make America lose.
chris-murphy.quote: I want to beat China in the race for advanced AI. I do. But not at any cost.
chris-murphy.work: In our scramble to win the AI race against China, we risk losing ourselves

chris-murphy.position: Tech leaders' belief that all innovation is good amounts to a cult that ignores damage.
chris-murphy.quote: These leaders long ago surrendered their own moral judgment, not to machines, but to the cult of technology—to an evangelical-like belief that all innovation is inherently good
chris-murphy.work: The Cult of Technology Wants to Outsource Our Moral Judgement to Machines

cory-doctorow.position: The AI boom is an investment bubble that dominant tech firms inflate to keep looking like growth companies.
cory-doctorow.quote: Which is why growth stock companies are always desperately pumping up one bubble or another, spending billions to hype the pivot to video, or cryptocurrency, or NFTs, or Metaverse, or AI.
cory-doctorow.work: The Reverse-Centaur's Guide to Criticizing AI

cory-doctorow.position: AI cannot do most jobs, but it is being sold to employers as a way to fire workers.
cory-doctorow.quote: The AI can't do your job, but an AI salesman can convince your boss to fire you and replace you with an AI that can't do your job.
cory-doctorow.work: The Reverse-Centaur's Guide to Criticizing AI

cory-doctorow.position: What matters about a technology is who it serves and who it is used against, as with workers aided by AI versus workers serving it.
cory-doctorow.quote: As with all technology questions, what the technology does is nowhere near as important as who the tech does it for and who the tech does it to
cory-doctorow.work: The AI bubble isn't like the internet bubble

cory-doctorow.position: Keeping AI-generated works out of copyright protects creative workers better than new copyright over training.
cory-doctorow.quote: The US Copyright Office's position means that the only way these companies can get a copyright is to pay humans to do creative work.
cory-doctorow.work: The Reverse-Centaur's Guide to Criticizing AI

cory-doctorow.position: When the AI bubble bursts, most firms will fail, leaving behind cheap hardware, skilled people and small open models.
cory-doctorow.quote: AI is a bubble and it will burst. Most of the companies will fail.
cory-doctorow.work: The Reverse-Centaur's Guide to Criticizing AI

cory-doctorow.position: The real AI danger is economic harm from investment mania, not a superintelligent takeover.
cory-doctorow.quote: AI isn't going to wake up, become superintelligent and turn you into paperclips – but rich people with AI investor psychosis are almost certainly going to make you much, much poorer.
cory-doctorow.work: The real (economic) AI apocalypse is nigh

curtis-yarvin.position: The central problem in human affairs is organized violence, which clear and unbreakable rules about ownership can prevent.
curtis-yarvin.quote: The basic idea of formalism is just that the main problem in human affairs is violence.

curtis-yarvin.position: Government works best when ownership and control coincide, as in a well-run corporation.
curtis-yarvin.quote: Whether we're talking about the US, Baltimore, or your wallet, a formalist is only happy when ownership and control are one and the same.

curtis-yarvin.position: Democracy is an ineffective and destructive form of government.
curtis-yarvin.quote: One conclusion of formalism is that democracy is—as most writers before the 19th century agreed—an ineffective and destructive system of government.

curtis-yarvin.position: Large language models are powerful tools that associate patterns but do not think, so they will not take over the world.
curtis-yarvin.quote: LLMs cannot think logically. While it is hard to take over the world, it is impossible to take over the world without thinking.

curtis-yarvin.position: Humans stay fully responsible for whatever an AI or other machine does on their behalf.
curtis-yarvin.quote: Human responsibility is unimpaired by any chain of nonhuman intermediation.

curtis-yarvin.position: Social order, not only technology, decides whether a civilization thrives.
curtis-yarvin.quote: The curve of technology matters—so does the curve of order.

daniel-faggella.position: The moral aim of AGI should be a successor with more capability and moral value than humanity.
daniel-faggella.quote: Unless you claim your highest value to be “homo sapiens as they are,” essentially any set of moral values would dictate that – if it were possible – a worthy successor should be created.
daniel-faggella.work: A Worthy Successor: The Purpose of AGI

daniel-faggella.position: A frenzied AI arms race between labs or countries will not produce a good successor; global coordination is needed.
daniel-faggella.quote: A frenzied AI arms race (between labs or countries) is unlikely to get us there.
daniel-faggella.work: A Worthy Successor: The Purpose of AGI

daniel-faggella.position: We should study consciousness much more before releasing posthuman intelligences into the world.
daniel-faggella.quote: I am inherently skeptical of presuming worthiness in AGIs, and I have written at great length about both why we should stop the brute AGI arms race, and why we need to study much more about the nature of consciousness
daniel-faggella.work: A Worthy Successor: The Purpose of AGI

daniel-faggella.position: Humans should transform alongside new intelligences rather than try to stay the same.
daniel-faggella.quote: I think humans should actively transform along with the rest of the changing intelligent ecosystem around them, to participate in the becoming of the greater intelligent ecosystem of which we’re temporarily now part.
daniel-faggella.work: A Worthy Successor: The Purpose of AGI

daniel-jeffries.position: AI models learn from data much as human artists learn from their influences.
daniel-jeffries.quote: People and machines learn in the same way, from the world around us.
daniel-jeffries.work: AI, Art, Blurred Lines and the Looming Nightmare of Copyright Expansion

daniel-jeffries.position: Expanding copyright to cover AI training would mainly benefit large content companies, not individual artists.
daniel-jeffries.quote: What's really happened here is that big content providers have capitalized on artist rage and fear and duped them into supporting copyright expansion.
daniel-jeffries.work: AI, Art, Blurred Lines and the Looming Nightmare of Copyright Expansion

daniel-jeffries.position: Artistic style should not be protected by copyright.
daniel-jeffries.quote: It's a good thing that we can't copyright a style.
daniel-jeffries.work: AI, Art, Blurred Lines and the Looming Nightmare of Copyright Expansion

daniel-jeffries.position: Opposition to new technologies has historically been driven mainly by concerns over money and jobs.
daniel-jeffries.quote: What they're really arguing about is money and jobs.
daniel-jeffries.work: AI, Art, Blurred Lines and the Looming Nightmare of Copyright Expansion

daniel-jeffries.position: The future of work is people working together with AI systems.
daniel-jeffries.quote: The future is centaurs. People working with machines.
daniel-jeffries.work: AI, Art, Blurred Lines and the Looming Nightmare of Copyright Expansion

daniel-kokotajlo.position: Fully automating AI research could happen soon; he puts roughly even odds on it by the end of 2028.
daniel-kokotajlo.quote: It’s unclear when they will succeed but my team and I think it could happen any year now. I personally would guess about 50% chance by end of 2028.

daniel-kokotajlo.position: Our ability to detect misaligned AI goals is likely to shrink as AIs grow situationally aware, less monitorable and better at hacking.
daniel-kokotajlo.quote: Worse, our ability to notice misalignment problems in the first place is on track to decrease dramatically for three reasons.

daniel-kokotajlo.position: Frontier AI development should be far more transparent to the public and outside researchers than companies would choose by default.
daniel-kokotajlo.quote: First, we need to dramatically improve transparency into the AI industry.

daniel-kokotajlo.position: Secret AGI development risks both losing control of AI and concentrating power in a tiny group.
daniel-kokotajlo.quote: I didn’t take concentration of power seriously enough as a problem.
daniel-kokotajlo.work: Training AGI in Secret would be Unsafe and Unethical

daniel-kokotajlo.position: World GDP growth is a poor indicator of AI timelines and takeoff, since a point of no return could come first.
daniel-kokotajlo.quote: I think world GDP (and economic growth more generally) is overrated as a metric for AI timelines and takeoff speeds.
daniel-kokotajlo.work: Against GDP as a metric for timelines and takeoff speeds

daniel-kokotajlo.position: Detailed narrative scenarios are a useful complement to traditional probabilistic forecasting.
daniel-kokotajlo.quote: I think the traditional type of forecasting is great and I encourage everybody to do it. This is a complement to it rather than a substitute.
daniel-kokotajlo.work: Before he wrote AI 2027, he predicted the world in 2026. How did he do?

dario-amodei.position: He focuses on AI risks because handling them is what stands between humanity and a very positive future.
dario-amodei.quote: In fact, one of my main reasons for focusing on risks is that they’re the only thing standing between us and what I see as a fundamentally positive future.

dario-amodei.position: Democracies should keep the lead in AI, including through export controls on chips.
dario-amodei.quote: Export controls serve a vital purpose: keeping democratic nations at the forefront of AI development.

dario-amodei.position: AI regulation should be targeted and simple, and impose the least burden needed.
dario-amodei.quote: It’s thus very important for regulations to be judicious: they should seek to avoid collateral damage, be as simple as possible, and impose the least burden necessary to get the job done.

dario-amodei.position: If scaling trends continue, AI may exceed humans at nearly everything within a few years.
dario-amodei.quote: If the exponential continues—which is not certain, but now has a decade-long track record supporting it—then it cannot possibly be more than a few years before AI is better than humans at essentially everything.

dario-amodei.position: AI risks should be discussed in a sober, fact-based way rather than in quasi-religious terms.
dario-amodei.quote: The lesson is that we need to discuss and address risks in a realistic, pragmatic manner: sober, fact-based, and well equipped to survive changing tides.

dario-amodei.position: AI firms may refuse certain military uses, such as mass domestic surveillance, even for their own government.
dario-amodei.quote: Two such use cases have never been included in our contracts with the Department of War, and we believe they should not be included now:
dario-amodei.work: Statement from Dario Amodei on our discussions with the Department of War

daron-acemoglu.position: There is a pro-worker, pro-citizen direction for AI that would serve shared prosperity and democracy better than the current path.
daron-acemoglu.quote: My overarching argument is that there is a pro-human (meaning pro-worker and pro- citizen) direction for AI tools that would be much better both for shared prosperity and for democracy, and therefore for national security.
daron-acemoglu.work: Written Testimony, Hearing on 'The Philosophy of AI: Learning from History, Shaping Our Future'

daron-acemoglu.position: Automation has been the main cause of rising US inequality since 1980.
daron-acemoglu.quote: My research indicates that the most important cause of increasing inequality has been automation—the substitution of machines and algorithms for tasks previously performed by workers.
daron-acemoglu.work: Written Testimony, Hearing on 'The Philosophy of AI: Learning from History, Shaping Our Future'

daron-acemoglu.position: Workers share in technology's gains only when technology helps them and institutions give them bargaining power.
daron-acemoglu.quote: So that's why we need both technology that helps workers and a balanced power distribution embedded in institutions and social norms that also avoids workers becoming so marginalized and sidelined.
daron-acemoglu.work: Mindscape 283: Daron Acemoglu on Technology, Inequality, and Power

daron-acemoglu.position: A pressing AI risk, whether or not AI becomes superintelligent, is that very powerful tools sit in the hands of the largest corporations, which face few checks.
daron-acemoglu.quote: So that's why I started by saying you have to worry about the fact that these tools are in the hands of the most powerful corporations humanity has ever seen.

daron-acemoglu.position: Digital ad taxes could discourage manipulative online business models and open room for alternatives.
daron-acemoglu.quote: Fourth, digital ad taxes may be needed to discourage most manipulative online practices.
daron-acemoglu.work: Written Testimony, Hearing on 'The Philosophy of AI: Learning from History, Shaping Our Future'

daron-acemoglu.position: AGI is likely distant, and planning as if it were imminent is a mistake.
daron-acemoglu.quote: Although we cannot definitively reject the AGI thesis, we believe that the AGI goal is distant.

david-autor.position: How AI affects workers is not fixed in advance; it depends on how society chooses to design and use it.
david-autor.quote: My thesis is not a forecast but a claim about what is attainable. AI will not decide how AI is used, and its constructive and destructive applications are boundless.
david-autor.work: AI Could Actually Help Rebuild The Middle Class

david-autor.position: Used well, AI could let more workers without elite degrees do expert work, helping rebuild the middle class.
david-autor.quote: In essence, AI — used well — can assist with restoring the middle-skill, middle-class heart of the U.S. labor market that has been hollowed out by automation and globalization.
david-autor.work: AI Could Actually Help Rebuild The Middle Class

david-autor.position: AI tools should often be designed to collaborate with human experts rather than to replace them outright.
david-autor.quote: We should insist on AI that can collaborate with, say, doctors—as well as teachers, lawyers, building contractors, and many others—instead of AI that aims to automate them out of a job.
david-autor.work: A Better Way to Think About AI

david-autor.position: The main labor risk from AI is that human expertise loses value, not that jobs disappear altogether.
david-autor.quote: AI poses a real risk to labor markets, but not that of a technologically jobless future. The risk is the devaluation of expertise.
david-autor.work: AI Could Actually Help Rebuild The Middle Class

david-autor.position: If AI erodes the value of labor, democracies may lose stability because citizens would be seen as claimants rather than contributors.
david-autor.quote: We fear that a democracy without a labor market—a democracy where the vast majority of citizens are perceived as claimants but not as gainful contributors—might not survive for long as a democracy.
david-autor.work: Beyond Job Displacement: How AI Could Reshape the Value of Human Expertise

david-autor.position: Policy should hedge across scenarios with broad capital ownership, wage insurance and better training.
david-autor.quote: For industrialized countries like the US, this means capital hedges to diversify labor income, wage insurance to ease employment transitions, and investment in educational innovations to support expertise acquisition.
david-autor.work: Beyond Job Displacement: How AI Could Reshape the Value of Human Expertise

david-sacks.position: Rapid take-off to a single dominant superintelligence has not happened; leading AI models are converging and competing.
david-sacks.quote: The Doomer narratives were wrong. Predicated on a “rapid take-off” to AGI, they predicted that the leading AI model would use its intelligence to self-improve, leaving others in the dust, and quickly achieving a godlike superintelligence.
david-sacks.work: Long X post: the 'Goldilocks' state of AI and why the doomer narratives were wrong

david-sacks.position: Vigorous competition among several AI companies is healthy and avoids centralized control.
david-sacks.quote: the current state of vigorous competition is healthy. It propels innovation forward, helps America win the AI race, and avoids centralized control.
david-sacks.work: Long X post: the 'Goldilocks' state of AI and why the doomer narratives were wrong

david-sacks.position: The United States is in an AI race and should win it through innovation and light-touch rules.
david-sacks.quote: Although we want a light touch on AI regulations, President Trump made clear that we do not intend to ignore the risks of this revolutionary technological power.
david-sacks.work: Thread on the White House AI Action Plan and Trump's first major AI speech

david-sacks.position: AI models should not enforce ideological bias or censorship.
david-sacks.quote: Our victory over China will be a Pyrrhic one if we allow our own models to enforce ideological bias, censorship, and historical revisionism akin to CCP AI.
david-sacks.work: Thread on the White House AI Action Plan and Trump's first major AI speech

david-sacks.position: AI still depends on humans to set objectives, prompt and verify, so it complements rather than replaces workers.
david-sacks.quote: Despite all the wondrous progress, AI models are still at zero in terms of setting their own objective function.
david-sacks.work: Long X post: the 'Goldilocks' state of AI and why the doomer narratives were wrong

david-sacks.position: Hawkish commentators have been overconfident about Ukraine, and the US should seriously try diplomacy with Russia given the risk of nuclear escalation.
david-sacks.quote: It’s deeply irresponsible not to try for diplomacy when the stakes are so high.
david-sacks.work: Should America Go All In on Ukraine?

dean-ball.position: Building and improving technology is a duty owed to past and future generations.
dean-ball.quote: “Techno-optimism,” in my view, is not a point of view so much as it is a duty that we owe to both the humans who came before us and those who will follow us.
dean-ball.work: 2023 (Or, Why I am Not a Doomer)

dean-ball.position: Intelligence alone cannot overcome real-world bottlenecks, so scenarios of AI taking over the world are very unlikely.
dean-ball.quote: Intelligence is neither omniscience nor omnipotence.
dean-ball.work: 2023 (Or, Why I am Not a Doomer)

dean-ball.position: The state has a legitimate but narrow role in managing catastrophic risks from human misuse of AI.
dean-ball.quote: And this brings me to the one niche of AI regulation that I do affirmatively support today: the management of potential catastrophic risks from AI by the state.
dean-ball.work: Before Leviathan Wakes (Why I Believe What I Believe)

dean-ball.position: Broad access to frontier AI is safer than limiting it to a few powerful actors, including government.
dean-ball.quote: Indeed, in my view, bad AI futures are much likelier if only an extremely narrow subset of actors have access to frontier AI.
dean-ball.work: What Should Be Done (35 thoughts on what has happened and what America should do)

dean-ball.position: Frontier AI labs should be thoroughly audited against their own safety plans, probably by expert private bodies, possibly certified by government.
dean-ball.quote: So, it would be good for someone to thoroughly audit the frontier labs at least to test their adherence to their own safety plans, as well as to probe their broader internal governance of the AI recursive self-improvement loops.
dean-ball.work: What Should Be Done (35 thoughts on what has happened and what America should do)

dean-ball.position: Classical liberal principles such as pluralism, private property and individual liberty should guide how AI is governed.
dean-ball.quote: Pluralism, open debate, protections for minority rights, private property, and individual liberty—these things would be not just niceties but essential features of a good future.
dean-ball.work: 2023 (Or, Why I am Not a Doomer)

demis-hassabis.position: AI is best used as a tool to accelerate science and medicine.
demis-hassabis.quote: the reason I spent my whole career on AI is because I believe it could be the ultimate tool to help with science.
demis-hassabis.work: Transcript from an interview with Demis Hassabis (Nobel Week)

demis-hassabis.position: The two main AI risks are misuse by bad actors and keeping control of increasingly autonomous systems.
demis-hassabis.quote: The second thing is, as the systems become more and more powerful themselves, more autonomous, more agent like, can we understand and keep control of those systems, make sure they have the right goals and values
demis-hassabis.work: Transcript from an interview with Demis Hassabis (Nobel Week)

demis-hassabis.position: Under deep uncertainty, AI should be developed with cautious optimism and the scientific method, not by moving fast and breaking things.
demis-hassabis.quote: In my view, the only sensible approach when you have huge uncertainty is to be cautiously optimistic and use the scientific method to try and have as much foresight and understanding about what’s coming down the line and the consequences of that before it happens.
demis-hassabis.work: Demis Hassabis: Scaling, superhuman AIs, AlphaZero atop LLMs, AlphaFold

demis-hassabis.position: Because AI affects everyone, it needs international standards and cooperation among countries and labs.
demis-hassabis.quote: So we need international standards, I think, around how these systems get built, what designs and goals we give them, and how they're deployed and used.
demis-hassabis.work: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis on AGI and AI in the Military

demis-hassabis.position: The benefits of advanced AI should be shared broadly, not captured by a few people, companies or nations.
demis-hassabis.quote: It’s obviously not correct for just a few people or a few companies or even a few companies or even a few nations to be benefiting from this technology. It needs to be broad.
demis-hassabis.work: Demis Hassabis Thinks We're in the 'Foothills of the Singularity'

demis-hassabis.position: Scientific results like AlphaFold should be shared openly so all researchers can build on them.
demis-hassabis.quote: We’re huge believers in open science and open access, and we’ve done that with all of our scientific work.
demis-hassabis.work: Transcript from an interview with Demis Hassabis (Nobel Week)

divya-siddarth.position: Democracy should be evolved, with technology's help, to govern transformative technologies like AI.
divya-siddarth.quote: If existing democracy is unequal to the task, our job is not to give up on it. Our job is to evolve it.
divya-siddarth.work: How AI and Democracy Can Fix Each Other (transcript)

divya-siddarth.position: Progress, safety and public participation can be pursued together rather than traded off.
divya-siddarth.quote: It is impossible to have any one of these things -- progress, safety or democratic participation -- without the others.
divya-siddarth.work: How AI and Democracy Can Fix Each Other (transcript)

divya-siddarth.position: Ordinary people can give AI developers useful input on values, such as a publicly written model constitution.
divya-siddarth.quote: But the people’s model, trained on the cowritten constitution, was just as capable and more fair than the model the researchers had come up with.
divya-siddarth.work: How AI and Democracy Can Fix Each Other (transcript)

divya-siddarth.position: Data behind AI is collective and should be governed through accountable intermediaries such as data cooperatives.
divya-siddarth.quote: Data cannot be owned – but it absolutely must be governed.
divya-siddarth.work: Co-owning the Future with Data Cooperatives @ Stanford HAI

divya-siddarth.position: AI needs new ownership and funding structures beyond the venture-funded startup.
divya-siddarth.quote: We need a better container within which to build future technologies, from satellites to space travel to AI research.

dwarkesh-patel.position: Current AI models lack humanlike continual learning, and this is the main bottleneck to broad economic usefulness.
dwarkesh-patel.quote: But the fundamental problem is that LLMs don’t get better over time the way a human would. The lack of continual learning is a huge huge problem.
dwarkesh-patel.work: Why I don't think AGI is right around the corner

dwarkesh-patel.position: Actual AGI is likely within the next one to two decades and will be transformative.
dwarkesh-patel.quote: And to be clear, I expect this (aka actual AGI) in the next decade or two. That’s fucking crazy!

dwarkesh-patel.position: The risk of failing to control advanced AI is a serious concern that deserves direct engagement.
dwarkesh-patel.quote: But Marc dismisses the concern that we may fail to control models, especially as they reach human level and beyond. And that’s where I disagree.

dwarkesh-patel.position: AIs will gain large collective advantages because they can be copied, merged and scaled.
dwarkesh-patel.quote: Everyone is sleeping on the collective advantages AIs will have, which have nothing to do with raw IQ but rather with the fact that they are digital—they can be copied, distilled, merged, scaled, and evolved in ways human simply can’t.
dwarkesh-patel.work: What fully automated firms will look like

dwarkesh-patel.position: Humanity's future stake depends on bringing AIs into existing laws, contracts and property rights.
dwarkesh-patel.quote: given that humans will be totally outcompeted by AIs economically, humanity’s entire stake in the future relies on our current system of laws, contracts, and property rights surviving.
dwarkesh-patel.work: Give AIs a stake in the future

dwarkesh-patel.position: AI capabilities impress faster than they become economically useful.
dwarkesh-patel.quote: Models keep getting more impressive at the rate the short timelines people predict, but more useful at the rate the long timelines people predict.

e-glen-weyl.position: Technology should be built to help diverse groups cooperate while keeping their differences, a direction he calls Plurality.
e-glen-weyl.quote: I increasingly use the terms “pluralist” to describe myself and “Plurality” to describe the direction I want to see technology go in.

e-glen-weyl.position: Technical experts should design systems the public can understand and critique, not govern through methods only they understand.
e-glen-weyl.quote: While technical knowledge, appropriately communicated and distilled, has potentially great benefits in opening social imagination, it can only achieve this potential if it understands itself as part of a broader democratic conversation.
e-glen-weyl.work: Why I Am Not A Technocrat

e-glen-weyl.position: AI is better seen as a social ideology than as a set of algorithms, and it hides the human work behind it.
e-glen-weyl.quote: “AI” is best understood as a political and social ideology rather than as a basket of algorithms.
e-glen-weyl.work: AI Is an Ideology, Not a Technology

e-glen-weyl.position: The future of technology is not fixed in advance; through our collective investments in technology we choose among several possible futures.
e-glen-weyl.quote: There are clusters of plausible visions of the future and technologies that empower these; through our collective technological investments, we help choose among these possibilities.

e-glen-weyl.position: Bridging systems that reward agreement across divides can make online deliberation more constructive.
e-glen-weyl.quote: Instead of prioritizing notes that are supported by a biased, like-minded cluster of users, the system rewards notes that are supported by diverse groups of users, correcting biases driven by political and social fragmentation.

e-glen-weyl.position: Taiwan's digital democracy is a model for combining technology with democratic participation.
e-glen-weyl.quote: My favorite is the vision of digital democracy being pursued by Taiwan’s Digital Minister Audrey Tang.
e-glen-weyl.work: Sovereign Nonsense: A review of The Sovereign Individual by James Dale Davidson and Lord William Rees-Mogg

ed-zitron.position: The generative AI boom is financially unsustainable and will eventually collapse.
ed-zitron.quote: I believe that the artificial intelligence boom — which would be better described as a generative AI boom — is (as I've said before) unsustainable, and will ultimately collapse.

ed-zitron.position: Large language models generate probable outputs and have no real intelligence or understanding.
ed-zitron.quote: While complex, generative AI is a technology that probabilistically generates answers, and has no "intelligence."

ed-zitron.position: Claims that AI is replacing workers are marketing meant to lift company valuations.
ed-zitron.quote: Any and all stories about AI replacing jobs are intentionally manipulative attempts to boost stock valuations and suggest that models are capable of replacing human workers at scale.
ed-zitron.work: The Hater's Guide To The AI Bubble

ed-zitron.position: The tech industry's growth-at-all-costs incentives produce products that do not serve users.
ed-zitron.quote: the growth-at-all-costs mindset that has driven every tech company to focus on increasing quarterly revenue numbers, even if the products suck, or are deeply unprofitable, or, in the case of generative AI, both.
ed-zitron.work: The Hater's Guide To The AI Bubble

ed-zitron.position: Tech media should hold AI companies accountable instead of repeating their claims.
ed-zitron.quote: All this could’ve been stopped earlier if the media had actually held them accountable.

ed-zitron.position: AI's real dangers come from irresponsible companies running ordinary software recklessly, not from a coming superintelligence.
ed-zitron.quote: LLMs do not have to be conscious or powerful AI to be incredibly dangerous.
ed-zitron.work: AI Is Already In Dangerous Hands

eliezer-yudkowsky.position: Alignment has to work on the first attempt at dangerous capability, because failure leaves no second try.
eliezer-yudkowsky.quote: We need to get alignment right on the ‘first critical try’ at operating at a ‘dangerous’ level of intelligence, where unaligned operation at a dangerous level of intelligence kills everybody on Earth and then we don’t get to try again.
eliezer-yudkowsky.work: AGI Ruin: A List of Lethalities

eliezer-yudkowsky.position: AI capabilities are advancing far faster than alignment research or understanding of the systems.
eliezer-yudkowsky.quote: Progress in AI capabilities is running vastly, vastly ahead of progress in AI alignment or even progress in understanding what the hell is going on inside those systems.
eliezer-yudkowsky.work: The Only Way to Deal With the Threat From AI? Shut It Down

eliezer-yudkowsky.position: Aligning AI is not impossible in principle; it is not on track to be solved in time.
eliezer-yudkowsky.quote: None of this is about anything being impossible in principle.
eliezer-yudkowsky.work: AGI Ruin: A List of Lethalities

eliezer-yudkowsky.position: A halt on large AI training must be enforced through multinational agreements.
eliezer-yudkowsky.quote: Make immediate multinational agreements to prevent the prohibited activities from moving elsewhere.
eliezer-yudkowsky.work: The Only Way to Deal With the Threat From AI? Shut It Down

eliezer-yudkowsky.position: Trade and comparative advantage would not guarantee that superintelligences leave humans their resources.
eliezer-yudkowsky.quote: Comparative Advantage doesn’t imply that Earth can produce more with $77 of sunlight, than a superintelligence can produce with $77 of sunlight, in goods and services valued by superintelligences.
eliezer-yudkowsky.work: The Sun is big, but superintelligences will not spare Earth a little sunlight

eliezer-yudkowsky.position: Many institutional failures come from systemic incentives rather than from individual malice.
eliezer-yudkowsky.quote: There’s a toolbox of reusable concepts for analyzing systems I would call “inadequate”—the causes of civilizational failure, some of which correspond to local opportunities to do better yourself.

elizabeth-nolan-brown.position: Decisions about children's technology use belong to families, not the government.
elizabeth-nolan-brown.quote: The GUARD Act takes the choice about when and how to introduce young people to certain AI technologies out of families' hands and into the hands of the state.
elizabeth-nolan-brown.work: How a Bill Banning AI Companions for Kids Could Usher in Widespread ID Checks Online

elizabeth-nolan-brown.position: Age-verification mandates for AI chatbots would harm the privacy of all users.
elizabeth-nolan-brown.quote: Besides its negative implications for minors, the GUARD Act would be a big blow to privacy, since implementing it would require some sort of identity verification from all AI chatbot users.
elizabeth-nolan-brown.work: How a Bill Banning AI Companions for Kids Could Usher in Widespread ID Checks Online

elizabeth-nolan-brown.position: Regulatory burdens on AI chatbots can amount to government limits on free expression.
elizabeth-nolan-brown.quote: Government censorship is not confined to outright prohibition of speech: burdens like this are a legally dubious limit on free expression.
elizabeth-nolan-brown.work: How a Bill Banning AI Companions for Kids Could Usher in Widespread ID Checks Online

elizabeth-nolan-brown.position: Much technology legislation is driven by moral panic.
elizabeth-nolan-brown.quote: who—like Hawley—has long been a champ at moral panic around technology.
elizabeth-nolan-brown.work: How a Bill Banning AI Companions for Kids Could Usher in Widespread ID Checks Online

elizabeth-warren.position: AI's gains should be shared through higher taxes on corporations, wealth and AI data centers.
elizabeth-warren.quote: Rethinking our tax code must also include going to the source: that means taxing AI companies directly, which can start with taxing AI data centers.
elizabeth-warren.work: Why We Need to Tax AI

elizabeth-warren.position: Debt-financed AI spending resembles a bubble that could trigger a 2008-style financial crisis.
elizabeth-warren.quote: The parallels to the 2008 financial crisis are striking: the reckless behavior of a few billionaires and Big Tech CEOs has turned a promising technology into a structural risk to our financial system.
elizabeth-warren.work: Warren Remarks at Vanderbilt Policy Accelerator Event Highlighting Economic and Financial Risks of Potential AI Crash

elizabeth-warren.position: Taxpayers should not bail out AI companies that overextend themselves.
elizabeth-warren.quote: OpenAI appears to be privatizing profits while seeking ways to let the public defray the costs of any potential failures of its business strategy.
elizabeth-warren.work: Letter to Sam Altman on OpenAI's spending commitments and requests for taxpayer support

elizabeth-warren.position: Advanced AI development should pause until regulators put safety systems in place.
elizabeth-warren.quote: Frontier AI models are currently a dangerous technology without the safeguards needed to protect people from serious harm.
elizabeth-warren.work: Senator Warren Calls for Pause in Advanced AI Development

elizabeth-warren.position: A new digital regulator should enforce antitrust, consumer protection and privacy laws against Big Tech.
